messages:
matt (Customer): Hey team — embeddings endpoint started returning vectors of length 1536 for us after switching to the TS SDK batching helper. Our model expects 512 and downstream indexing fails with a dimension mismatch. Anyone seen this?
jamie (Support): Sorry you're hitting that. Can you paste a minimal repro (SDK call + an example response) and the exact model you requested?
matt (Customer): Using python sdk v0.9.2 and model `open-embed-512`. Minimal call:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key="***", batcher_config={"enabled": True, "max_batch_size": 16})
resp = c.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-512", input=["hello world", "foo bar"])
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))
```
Response snippet:
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, 0.002, ..., /* total 1536 floats */]}], "model":"open-embed-512"}
```
We get 1536 on every vector. The client retry logic also shows a 504 occasionally when batching >8.
jamie (Support): Thanks — that helps. Can you run with `batcher_config={"enabled": False}` or `max_batch_size":1}` to confirm if batching is involved?
matt (Customer): Yup. With batcher disabled I get 512. So it's definitely something about the batched request path.
sasha (SDK): Thanks for the repro, Matt. Quick note: TS/JS batching shims did a change last week to route some models to the v2 embeddings path that returns 1536 dims (backwards compat bug). We'll triage. Can you share the full request payload (headers + body) when batching is enabled? Ops-bot trace ID would help too.
matt (Customer): Full request body (redacted api_key):

POST /v1/embeddings/batch
Headers: Authorization: Bearer ***, Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  "model": "open-embed-512",
  "inputs": ["hello world", "foo bar"],
  "batch_id": "b-934"
}

And the response headers included `x-request-trace: tx-9f8c` and `x-runtime: 0.34s`. No explicit error in body, just the wrong vector length.
kris (Infra): pinging infra logs for tx-9f8c. Also, matt, approx QPS when this happens? Does it only occur on batched calls or any batch size >1?
matt (Customer): Low QPS (<<10 qps). Repro is trivial locally by running the python snippet above.
sasha (SDK): Potential cause: batching path was defaulting to a different model alias (open-embed-1536) for compatibility. Workaround pushed: set `client.embeddings.create(..., model="open-embed-512@strict")` or disable batching. We'll patch the alias mapping in next release.
jamie (Support): I'm opening an internal ticket with priority P1 for SDK/Runtime teams. Ticket: RED-7321. Attaching the traces and your repro. In the meantime, please use the `@strict` suffix or disable client batching as Sasha suggested.
kris (Infra): Found trace tx-9f8c: router forwarded batched request to a different backend pool that serves multi-dim (1536) embeddings for `open-embed` family. We'll add a router rule to preserve explicit model variant for batched flows.
matt (Customer): Thanks — the `@strict` suffix fixed it for now. One more thing: the client retry backoff + batcher was re-sending whole batches on 504 which caused duplicate downstream requests. Any recommended client-side mitigation?
sasha (SDK): Short-term: set `retry_config = {"max_retries":2, "retry_on": [429, 502], "disable_batch_retry": True}` in your client config. We'll add finer-grained batch retry semantics in next SDK patch so partial-batch retries are safer.
jamie (Support): Closing loop: workaround confirmed, internal ticket open, ETA for SDK patch: 48–72 hours. Infra will deploy router rule in next hour. I'll update this thread when fixes land. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident RED-7321 created and linked to trace tx-9f8c. SLA timer started.
matt (Customer): Appreciated — will hold off on rolling to production until confirmed. Cheers.
